title: Quantitative Analysis of the Arabidopsis Leaf Secretory Proteome via TMT-Based Mass Spectrometry
author: Sakharam Waghmare
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Arabidopsis thaliana Columbia-0 ecotype (Col-0, ABRC stock CS
and transgenic lines; store seeds at 4 °C in dry conditions for maximum viability Reagents
Sodium dodecyl sulphate (SDS) (Sigma-Aldrich, catalog number: L
Gel stain (Neo Biotech, catalog number: NB-45-
Bradford protein assay dye reagent concentrate (Bio-Rad, catalog number:

steps.title: Grow Arabidopsis plants
steps.instruction: Sow ~50 Col‑0 seeds in 6.5 cm plastic pots filled with soil, cover with a tray and vernalize at 4 °C in the dark for 2–3 days; transfer to a growth chamber at 22 °C, 8 h light/16 h dark, 150 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ white light, 55–60 % RH for 8–10 days; transplant seedlings into 6.5 cm square pots with holes, cover and return to the chamber; after ~7 days uncover and grow two more weeks; plants are ready for apoplast collection when rosettes have 10–12 leaves (~20 days after planting).

steps.title: Infiltrate leaves and collect apoplast
steps.instruction: Fill a 1 mL needle‑less syringe with infiltration buffer, press the syringe on the abaxial side of each leaf while holding the adaxial side with a fingertip, allowing the buffer to spread uniformly through the whole leaf; slice leaves (without petioles), blot on tissue paper, stack 6–8 leaves, roll and load into a 10 mL syringe barrel‑down; place a 0.5 mL microfuge tube at the bottom of a 50 mL Falcon tube, insert the syringe barrel, close the tube and centrifuge at 750 × g for 4 min at 4 °C (fixed‑angle rotor); collect the apoplastic flush (~50–100 µL from six leaves), which should be colorless (green tint indicates cytosolic contamination).

steps.title: Determine protein concentration and denature
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration of the apoplastic flush with a Bradford assay; for MS use ~50 µL at ~1 µg µL⁻¹ (expected 0.5–2.5 µg µL⁻¹); add 1× Laemmli buffer to the sample and incubate at 95 °C for 5 min (pause point: store at –20 °C, noting that protein may precipitate in the infiltration solution); run an SDS‑PAGE gel to assess quality (absence of Rubisco large‑chain band confirms low cytoplasmic contamination; if >1 % contamination repeat centrifugation at lower speed or increase spin time).

steps.title: Filter‑aided sample preparation (FASP) digestion
steps.instruction: Reduce samples (Laemmli buffer: 95 °C 5 min; SDT‑lysis buffer: room temperature 30 min). In a 30 kDa cutoff filter unit, mix up to 50 µL apoplastic flush in Laemmli buffer with 200 µL UA and centrifuge 14,000 × g 15 min (repeat if volume remains). Add 200 µL UA, centrifuge 14,000 × g 15 min; discard flowthrough. Add 100 µL IAA solution, mix at 600 rpm in a thermo‑mixer for 1 min, incubate 20 min in the dark at room temperature; centrifuge 14,000 × g 10 min, discard flowthrough. Add 100 µL UA, centrifuge 14,000 × g 10 min; repeat this UA wash twice. Add 100 µL 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, centrifuge 14,000 × g 10 min; repeat twice. Add 120 µL 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate containing trypsin (enzyme‑to‑protein ratio 1:100, e.g., 0.25 µg trypsin for 25 µg protein), mix at 600 rpm 1 min, avoid bubbles; incubate at 37 °C for at least 4 h up to overnight. Transfer filter to a new collection tube and centrifuge 14,000 × g 10 min. Add 50 µL 10 % acetonitrile, centrifuge 14,000 × g 10 min, discard flowthrough. Add TFA to 1 % final concentration, dry the sample in a vacuum centrifuge. Reconstitute in 100 µL 100 mM TEAB, measure peptide concentration with a Nanodrop at 205 nm (expected 10–100 µg µL⁻¹). Store at –20 °C if needed.

steps.title: Label peptides with TMT
steps.instruction: Equilibrate 6‑plex TMT reagents to room temperature; for 0.8 mg vials add 41 µL anhydrous acetonitrile, for 5 mg vials add 256 µL solvent, vortex 5 min, briefly centrifuge. Add 8 µL TMT label to each 25 µL peptide aliquot (final acetonitrile 24 %); use 10–25 µg peptide per labeling. Incubate 1 h at room temperature, timing precisely for each channel. Quench by adding 8 µL 5 % hydroxylamine (final hydroxylamine 0.23 %) and incubate 15 min. Combine all labeled samples to a total of 3 µg in a 96‑well plate; store remaining material at –80 °C until QC. Dry the combined sample in a SpeedVac, then resuspend in 20 µL sample‑resuspension buffer. Proceed to mass spectrometry.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS analysis of TMT peptides
steps.instruction: Inject 5 µL of the resuspended TMT‑labeled sample onto an Orbitrap Elite/Fusion coupled to a Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLC nanoflow system. Desalt on a 0.3 × 5 mm trap column at 25 µL min⁻¹ with 1 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % formic acid for 10 min. Separate peptides on a PepMap C18 analytical column using solvent A (0.01 % FA) and solvent B (0.08 % FA, 80 % ACN) with the following gradient at 0.3 mL min⁻¹: 4 % B for 1.5 min, 4–60 % B over 178.5 min, 60–99 % B over 15 min, hold 99 % B for 5 min (total 210 min), then 10 min re‑equilibration at 4 % B. MS settings: MS1 – 120 000 resolution, m/z 375–1500; top‑speed 3 s HCD MS2 – 60 000 resolution; HCD energy/isolation: 2+ ions 40 % HCD, 1.2 m/z; 3+ ions 38 % HCD, 0.7 m/z; 4–6+ ions 38 % HCD, 0.5 m/z. Dynamic exclusion 45 s.

steps.title: Predict spectral libraries in Proteome Discoverer
steps.instruction: Download the Arabidopsis proteome (UniProt ID 3702) in FASTA format and split into four files (A–D). In Proteome Discoverer 3.0, add each FASTA file via the Administration start page. Open “Spectral Libraries”, click Predict, select a FASTA file, name the library and specify organism. Set parameters: activation HCD, collision energy 28, enzyme trypsin, peptide length 7–30, precursor charge 2–3, max missed cleavages 2, min precursor mass 2 Da. Define static modifications: Carbamidomethyl (C), TMT‑6‑plex (K, N‑terminus); dynamic modification: oxidation (M) with max 3 per peptide. Predict libraries for all four FASTA files.

steps.title: Process MS data in Proteome Discoverer
steps.instruction: Create a new Study/Analysis, name it, set root directory, choose processing and consensus workflows, and click OK. In Study Definition, add quantification method “TMT‑6plex”. Add raw MS files. Define study factors (biological replicates, categorical) as in the example (e.g., Lines for mutant/WT). On the Sample tab, set sample type (Control or Sample). Build processing and consensus workflows by dragging nodes; in the MSPepSearch node select the four Arabidopsis spectral libraries (A–D). In the Grouping and Quantification tab, generate Sample Groups using the categorical factor (Lines) to obtain mutant/WT ratios in a nested design. For secretory‑protein annotation, add the Arabidopsis protein database containing signal peptides, transmembrane domains, and ER‑retention signals as FASTA files, and select them in the Protein Marker node.
